questions.question:
Three points are given: P = (1, 2), Q = (4, 6), and R = (7, 2). Which of the following statements about triangle PQR are true?

Indicate all such statements.
options: B. Triangle PQR is a right triangle
C. The area of triangle PQR is 12 square units
D. The centroid of the triangle is at (4, 10/3)
E. PR is the longest side of the triangle
questions.trap: For option B, students only check PQ²+QR² vs PR² (one pairing) and stop when it fails, not realizing they must check all three pairings to confirm no right angle exists anywhere in the triangle.

questions.question:
Quantity A: The number of positive integers from 1 to 100 that are divisible by 3 or 5
Quantity B: 47
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Use inclusion-exclusion: |divisible by 3 or 5| = |div by 3| + |div by 5| − |div by 15|. |div by 3|: floor(100/3) = 33. |div by 5|: floor(100/5) = 20. |div by 15|: floor(100/15) = 6. Total = 33 + 20 − 6 = 47. Quantity A = 47 = Quantity B. Answer is C.
questions.trap: Students add 33 + 20 = 53 without subtracting the 6 numbers divisible by both (multiples of 15), overcounting by 6 and getting 53.

questions.question: A committee of 4 must be chosen from 6 men and 4 women, all 10 people distinct. The committee members hold no distinct roles, so order does not matter, and no person may serve twice. How many committees contain exactly 2 men and exactly 2 women?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — the committee is built from two separate pools, so choose from each pool and MULTIPLY.
Step 2 — men: C(6,2) = (6 x 5)/2 = 15.
Step 3 — women: C(4,2) = (4 x 3)/2 = 6.
Step 4 — total = 15 x 6 = 90.
Check the size: 90 is well under C(10,4) = 210, the number of committees with no composition requirement. Correct.
Answer: 90.
questions.trap: Choice A, 21, comes from ADDING the pools (15 + 6) instead of multiplying - but each of the 15 pairs of men can be paired with each of the 6 pairs of women, so the counts multiply. Choice B, 60, is C(6,2) x C(4,1) = 15 x 4, from choosing only one woman. Choice E, 210 = C(10,4), ignores the 2-and-2 requirement altogether, and choice D, 180, is P(6,2) x C(4,2) = 30 x 6, from ordering the two men.

questions.question:
Cone P has base radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. Cone Q has base radius 4 cm and height 3 cm.

Quantity A: Total surface area of Cone P
Quantity B: Total surface area of Cone Q
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Both cones have slant height l = √(r² + h²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. Cone P: SA = πr² + πrl = π(9) + π(3)(5) = 9π + 15π = 24π. Cone Q: SA = πr² + πrl = π(16) + π(4)(5) = 16π + 20π = 36π. Quantity B (36π) > Quantity A (24π).
questions.trap: Students notice both cones have the same slant height (5) and the same r + h sum (7), and conclude the surface areas are equal. They are not — both πr² and πrl depend heavily on r, and r = 4 gives a much larger surface area than r = 3.

questions.question:
EMPLOYEES SURVEYED AND MAIN WAY OF COMMUTING, BY SIZE OF FIRM
percents are of the employees surveyed at that size of firm

Note: Every employee surveyed reported exactly one main way of commuting.

Approximately how many of the employees surveyed at the small and medium firms combined do not commute mainly by car?
questions.explanation: At the small firms 30 percent do not drive: 0.30 x 360 = 108. At the medium firms 40 percent: 0.40 x 640 = 256. Together 364.
questions.trap: Students average the two car percentages to 65, apply a single 35 percent to the combined 1,000 employees and answer 350. The two firm sizes surveyed different numbers of people, so the percents cannot be averaged without weighting.

questions.question:
EMPLOYEES SURVEYED AND MAIN WAY OF COMMUTING, BY SIZE OF FIRM
percents are of the employees surveyed at that size of firm

Note: Every employee surveyed reported exactly one main way of commuting.

Approximately what percent of the employees surveyed at the small and large firms combined commute mainly by public transit?
questions.explanation: Public transit accounts for 0.10 x 360 = 36 at the small firms and 0.40 x 800 = 320 at the large firms, which is 356 out of 1160 employees: 0.3069, about 30.7 percent.
questions.trap: Students average 10 percent and 40 percent to get 25 percent. The large firms contributed more than twice as many employees, so the combined figure is pulled toward 40 percent.

questions.question:
EMPLOYEES SURVEYED AND MAIN WAY OF COMMUTING, BY SIZE OF FIRM
percents are of the employees surveyed at that size of firm

Note: Every employee surveyed reported exactly one main way of commuting.

Which of the following statements about the employees surveyed can be determined from the information given?

Indicate all such statements.
options: A. More employees commute mainly by car at the large firms than at the small firms.
B. Across all three sizes of firm, more than half of the employees surveyed commute mainly by car.
C. The number who bike or walk is the same at the medium firms as at the large firms.
D. At every size of firm, more employees commute mainly by car than by public transit.
E. More than 200 of the employees surveyed at the large firms bike or walk.
questions.explanation: Car: large 0.45 x 800 = 360 against small 0.70 x 360 = 252, so A holds. Across all three, car totals 996 of 1,800 surveyed, more than half, so B holds. Bike or walk: medium 0.15 x 640 = 96, large 0.15 x 800 = 120; equal percents of unequal totals are not equal counts, so C fails. Car exceeds public transit at every size (70 > 10, 60 > 25, 45 > 40), so D holds. Large bike or walk is 120, not more than 200, so the last fails.
questions.trap: Students accept the third statement because both firm sizes show 15 percent. The medium firms surveyed 650 employees and the large firms 800, so the same percent is a different number of people.

questions.question: The parabola y = x² + bx + c has its vertex on the line y = x. If the axis of symmetry is x = 3, what is the value of c?
questions.explanation: Step 1: Axis of symmetry is x = −b/2 = 3, so b = −6. Step 2: The vertex x-coordinate is 3. Since the vertex lies on y = x, the vertex y-coordinate equals 3. So the vertex is (3, 3). Step 3: Substitute (3, 3) into y = x² + bx + c: 3 = (3)² + (−6)(3) + c = 9 − 18 + c = −9 + c. Solve: c = 12.
questions.trap: Students compute c = b²/4 = 36/4 = 9, confusing c with the result of the vertex formula c − b²/(4a). The vertex y-value is c − b²/(4a) = c − 9, and setting this equal to 3 gives c = 12.

questions.question: x > 0, y > 0, (sqrt(x) + sqrt(y))^2 = 25, and xy = 36. What is the value of x + y?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — a power does not distribute over a sum, so expand with (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 taking a = sqrt(x) and b = sqrt(y).
Step 2 — the squared terms are (sqrt(x))^2 = x and (sqrt(y))^2 = y. The cross term is 2*sqrt(x)*sqrt(y) = 2*sqrt(xy), using sqrt(x)*sqrt(y) = sqrt(xy), which is valid because x and y are positive.
Step 3 — so the first condition reads x + y + 2*sqrt(xy) = 25. The expansion has turned the unknown pair into the two symmetric quantities x + y and xy, and the second condition supplies one of them.
Step 4 — substitute xy = 36: sqrt(xy) = sqrt(36) = 6, so the cross term is 2*6 = 12.
Step 5 — the equation becomes x + y + 12 = 25, so x + y = 13.
Check: x + y = 13 with xy = 36 means x and y are 4 and 9. Then (sqrt(4) + sqrt(9))^2 = (2 + 3)^2 = 25 and 4*9 = 36, so both conditions hold. Correct.
Answer: B.
questions.trap: Choice D drops the cross term altogether, distributing the square over the sum to get x + y = 25; the missing 12 is exactly that term. Choice C uses sqrt(xy) = 6 as the cross term but forgets to double it, subtracting 6 instead of 12. Choice A substitutes xy = 36 directly for the cross term, as though 2*sqrt(x)*sqrt(y) were xy, and 25 - 36 = -11 - a negative value that cannot be a sum of two positive numbers, which is the signal that the step was wrong. Choice E moves the 12 the wrong way, adding it to 25 instead of subtracting it.

questions.question:
A principal of $2,000 is invested for 2 years at 8 percent per year.
Quantity A: The total amount if the interest is simple
Quantity B: The total amount if the interest is compounded annually
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — Quantity A: A = 2000 * (1 + 0.08*2) = 2000 * 1.16 = 2320.
Step 2 — Quantity B: A = 2000 * (1.08)^2 = 2000 * 1.1664 = 2332.80.
Step 3 — the structural route needs no multiplication of the whole amount: over exactly 2 years the compound account beats the simple account by P*r^2 = 2000 * (0.08)^2 = 2000 * 0.0064 = 12.80, and 12.80 is positive, so Quantity B is greater.
Check: 2320 + 12.80 = 2332.80, matching Step 2. Correct.
Answer: B.
questions.trap: Answering C by recalling that simple and compound agree for one period and failing to notice that t = 2 here; the accounts are equal only after the first period. Answering D because 'the compounding frequency of the simple account is unstated' misreads the setup: simple interest has no compounding at all, so both columns are fully determined.

questions.question:
x and y are positive with x/y = 4/5.
Quantity A: (x + 4)/(y + 4)
Quantity B: x/y
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — x/y = 4/5 < 1, so x < y.
Step 2 — adding the same positive amount to the top and bottom of a fraction pulls it towards 1. Below 1, that means it goes UP.
Step 3 — test it with the smallest case, x = 4 and y = 5: (4 + 4)/(5 + 4) = 8/9 = 0.889, which is greater than 4/5 = 0.8.
Step 4 — test a scaled case, x = 40 and y = 50: 44/54 = 0.815, still greater than 0.8.
The direction never changes, so Quantity A is greater.
Proof if you want it: (x + 4)/(y + 4) - x/y = 4(y - x)/[y(y + 4)], which is positive whenever y > x.
questions.trap: Believing that adding the same number to both parts leaves a ratio alone - that is true for MULTIPLYING both parts, not adding. Note the rule has a direction: a fraction below 1 rises, a fraction above 1 falls, and both are moving towards 1.

questions.question: The table above shows how many of 50 inspected units had each possible number of defects. What is the average (arithmetic mean) number of defects per inspected unit?
questions.explanation: Weight each defect count by how many units had it. The total number of defects is 0(18) + 1(14) + 2(9) + 3(6) + 4(3) = 0 + 14 + 18 + 18 + 12 = 62. The 50 units share those 62 defects, so the average is 62/50 = 1.24 defects per unit.
questions.trap: A student who averages the five defect values in the left column, ignoring how many units fall in each row, computes (0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4)/5 = 2. The rows are far from equally populated, with 18 units at zero defects, so the weighted average is 1.24 rather than 2.

easy.question:
Circle C₁ has radius r₁ and circle C₂ has radius r₂, where r₁ + r₂ = 10.

Quantity A: Sum of the areas of C₁ and C₂
Quantity B: Area of a circle with radius 5
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation: Quantity B = π(5²) = 25π. Quantity A = π(r₁²) + π(r₂²) = π(r₁² + r₂²). We need to compare r₁² + r₂² with 25 given r₁ + r₂ = 10. By the identity (r₁+r₂)² = r₁²+r₂²+2r₁r₂: 100 = r₁²+r₂²+2r₁r₂ → r₁²+r₂² = 100−2r₁r₂. Because (r₁ − r₂)² ≥ 0, 4r₁r₂ ≤ (r₁+r₂)² = 100, so r₁r₂ ≤ 25. So r₁²+r₂² = 100−2r₁r₂ ≥ 100−50 = 50 > 25. Equality only when r₁ = r₂ = 5, but then Quantity A = π(25+25) = 50π > 25π = Quantity B. Quantity A is always strictly greater (≥ 50π > 25π).
easy.trap: Thinking that since r₁ + r₂ = 10 = 2×5, the sum of areas equals the area of one circle with radius 5. Area is not linear in radius.

easy.question: The integer j is the product of four different prime numbers. If the result when j is divided by 6 is a multiple of 5, which of the following could be the result when j is divided by 3?
easy.explanation: For j/6 to be an integer, j must include both 2 and 3 among its prime factors. For j/6 to be a multiple of 5, j must include 5 as well. So j = 2 x 3 x 5 x q, where q is a fourth prime different from 2, 3 and 5. Dividing by 3 leaves j/3 = 2 x 5 x q = 10q. Testing the options: 20 requires q = 2, 30 requires q = 3 and 50 requires q = 5 — each repeats a prime already used, violating 'four different primes'. 90 requires q = 9, which is not prime. 70 requires q = 7, a prime distinct from 2, 3 and 5, so j = 210 and j/3 = 70.
easy.trap: Students check only that the option is a multiple of 10 and choose the first one that qualifies, usually 20. The constraint doing the real work is the word 'different': q must be a prime that is not already a factor of j.

easy.question:
Segment AD has length 44. Point B lies on AD with BD = 19. Point C also lies on AD, and BC = 7.

Which of the following values the length AC could equal?

Indicate all such values.
easy.explanation:
AB = AD - BD = 44 - 19 = 25.
C is 7 units from B along AD, and it can sit on either side of B.
C on the A side of B: AC = AB - BC = 25 - 7 = 18. This is allowed because 7 <= 25.
C on the D side of B: AC = AB + BC = 25 + 7 = 32. This is allowed because 7 <= BD = 19, so C stays on the segment.
A: 12 = BD - BC is not a distance from A. FALSE.
B: 18 is possible. TRUE.
C: 25 would put C at B itself, but BC = 7. FALSE.
D: 32 is possible. TRUE.
E: 37 = 44 - 7 would measure from the wrong end. FALSE.
Answer: B, D.
easy.trap: Placing C on only one side of B, usually between B and D, so only 32 is found (choice D alone), or giving the distance AB itself as the answer (choice C).

easy.question:
Data set A: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50
Data set B is Data set A with the value 50 replaced by 500.
Quartiles are found by the standard method, with the median excluded from each half.
Quantity A: The interquartile range of Data set A
Quantity B: The interquartile range of Data set B
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — Data set A. Median = 30. Lower half {10, 20} gives Q1 = 15; upper half {40, 50} gives Q3 = 45. IQR = 45 - 15 = 30.
Step 2 — Data set B = 10, 20, 30, 40, 500. Median is still 30. Lower half {10, 20} still gives Q1 = 15; upper half is now {40, 500}, so Q3 = (40 + 500)/2 = 270.
Step 3 — IQR of B = 270 - 15 = 255.
Step 4 — 255 > 30, so Quantity B is greater.
Why the IQR moved so much: with only 5 values the upper half holds just two numbers, so the MAXIMUM is one of the two values averaged to make Q3. In a small data set the extreme value is a quartile ingredient.
easy.trap: Choosing C on the rule of thumb that the IQR ignores outliers. That rule holds when the data set is large enough that the extreme sits beyond the quartile positions; here n = 5 and Q3 = (v4 + v5)/2 uses the maximum directly, so replacing 50 with 500 drags Q3 from 45 to 270. Compare STA-IQR-029, where 9 values do keep the maximum out of Q3.

easy.question: n is an integer with -6 <= n <= 6. For how many of these values of n is the expression (n^4 - 13n^2 + 36)/(n^2 - 5n + 6) defined and not equal to 0?
easy.explanation:
Two conditions have to be imposed in the right order: defined (denominator not 0) and then non-zero (numerator not 0).
Step 1 — factor the numerator as a quadratic in n^2: n^4 - 13n^2 + 36 = (n^2 - 4)(n^2 - 9) = (n - 2)(n + 2)(n - 3)(n + 3). It vanishes at n = 2, -2, 3 and -3.
Step 2 — factor the denominator: n^2 - 5n + 6 = (n - 2)(n - 3). It vanishes at n = 2 and n = 3.
Step 3 — the range -6 to 6 holds 6 - (-6) + 1 = 13 integers.
Step 4 — remove the undefined values. At n = 2 and n = 3 the denominator is 0; the numerator is 0 there too, so the expression reads 0/0, which is undefined, not 0. 13 - 2 = 11 values are defined.
Step 5 — now remove the zeros from those 11. The numerator's remaining roots are n = -2 and n = -3, and both have non-zero denominators: at n = -2 the denominator is 4 + 10 + 6 = 20, at n = -3 it is 9 + 15 + 6 = 30. Each gives a defined value of exactly 0, so both are excluded: 11 - 2 = 9.
Check: n = 0 gives 36/6 = 6, defined and non-zero, so it survives - a zero value of n is not a zero value of the expression. The nine survivors are -6, -5, -4, -1, 0, 1, 4, 5 and 6. Correct.
Answer: D.
easy.trap: Answering 11 by imposing only the 'defined' condition and forgetting that n = -2 and n = -3 make the expression a perfectly defined 0. Answering 8 by also striking out n = 0 on reflex; there the expression is 36/6 = 6. Answering 7 by subtracting all four numerator roots after already subtracting n = 2 and n = 3 as undefined, removing those two twice (13 - 2 - 4). Answering 6 combines that double removal with striking out n = 0.

easy.question:
A and B are integers with A > B > 1.
Quantity A: P(A, B)
Quantity B: A x P(A - 1, B - 1)
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — write both sides with factorials.
P(A, B) = A!/(A - B)!
P(A - 1, B - 1) = (A - 1)!/((A - 1) - (B - 1))! = (A - 1)!/(A - B)!
Step 2 — multiply out Quantity B: A x (A - 1)!/(A - B)! = A!/(A - B)!, because A x (A - 1)! = A!.
Step 3 — the two expressions are the same, so the columns are equal for every A > B > 1.
Why it makes sense: filling the first of the B ordered slots (A ways) and then arranging B - 1 of the remaining A - 1 objects is the same job as arranging B of A objects.
Check A = 5, B = 3: P(5, 3) = 60 and 5 x P(4, 2) = 5 x 12 = 60. Check A = 7, B = 4: P(7, 4) = 840 and 7 x P(6, 3) = 7 x 120 = 840. Correct.
The two quantities are equal.
easy.trap: Testing one pair of values, seeing equality, then choosing D because A and B are unknown; the factorials cancel identically, so equality is forced for every admissible pair. The opposite slip is expanding P(A - 1, B - 1) as (A - 1)!/(A - B - 1)!, which mishandles the double shift, inflates Quantity B by a factor of A - B and points at B.

easy.question:
A data set consists of 6 distinct positive integers whose range is 10.
Quantity A: The greatest possible standard deviation of the data set
Quantity B: 5
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — set up the extreme case. SD does not change when the whole set slides, so take the smallest value to be 1; the range of 10 then forces the largest to be 11. Four more distinct integers must sit strictly between them.
Step 2 — to push the SD as high as possible, drive every value as far from the center as the distinctness rule allows: pack them against the two ends. The best arrangement is {1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 11}.
Step 3 — evaluate it. Mean = (1 + 2 + 3 + 9 + 10 + 11)/6 = 36/6 = 6.
Squared deviations: 25, 16, 9, 9, 16, 25. Sum = 100.
Variance = 100/6 = 16.67, so SD = sqrt(16.67) = 4.08.
Step 4 — compare. The greatest possible SD is about 4.08, which is less than 5, so Quantity B is greater.
Answer: B.
Why 5 is unreachable: even without the distinctness rule, the absolute ceiling on the SD of a set with range R is R/2 = 5, achieved only by putting every value at one of the two extremes. Six DISTINCT integers cannot do that, so the true maximum lands strictly below 5.
easy.trap: Reasoning that a range of 10 means values can be 5 from the center, so the SD 'could be' 5, and keying C. Reaching R/2 would require every value to sit exactly at an endpoint; distinctness forces four of the six inward, which drags the average squared deviation down to 100/6 and the SD to 4.08. Keying D on the grounds that the values are unnamed is the other slip - the stem asks for a maximum, and the maximum is a definite number.

easy.question:
An amount of $1,000 is invested at r percent per year, compounded annually, where r > 0.
Quantity A: The interest earned during the third year
Quantity B: Twice the interest earned during the first year
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — write the decimal rate as d = r/100, with d > 0.
Step 2 — the first year's interest is earned on the opening balance of 1,000: it is 1000*d.
Step 3 — the third year's interest is earned on the balance at the start of year 3, which is 1000*(1 + d)^2. So Quantity A = 1000*d*(1 + d)^2.
Step 4 — Quantity B = 2000*d. Dividing both columns by the positive quantity 1000*d, the comparison is (1 + d)^2 against 2.
Step 5 — (1 + d)^2 = 2 exactly when d = sqrt(2) - 1 = 0.4142, that is r = 41.42 percent.
Step 6 — test r = 10: (1.10)^2 = 1.21 < 2, so Quantity B is greater. Test r = 50: (1.50)^2 = 2.25 > 2, so Quantity A is greater. The relationship flips.
Check the two cases in dollars. At r = 10: year 1 interest 100, year 3 interest 1000*0.10*1.21 = 121, and Quantity B = 200 > 121. At r = 50: year 1 interest 500, year 3 interest 1000*0.50*2.25 = 1125, and Quantity B = 1000 < 1125. Correct.
Answer: D.
easy.trap: Answering B looks safe because at every ordinary bank rate the balance has not come close to doubling by year 3, so the third year's interest is well under twice the first year's. That reasoning quietly assumes r is small; the stem allows any r > 0, and above about 41.4 percent the balance more than doubles in two years and Quantity A wins. Answering A on the reflex 'compound interest grows fast' fails for exactly the same reason in the other direction.

easy.question: For real numbers u and v, let d(u, v) = |u - v|. If d(x, 3) + d(x, 7) = d(3, 7), which of the following must be true?
options: E. No real x satisfies the equation
easy.explanation:
Rewrite in ordinary notation: |x - 3| + |x - 7| = |3 - 7| = 4.
The left side is the distance from x to 3 plus the distance from x to 7; the right side is the distance from 3 to 7.
Step 1 — if 3 <= x <= 7, the two trips together cover the segment exactly once: (x - 3) + (7 - x) = 4. Every such x works, endpoints included.
Step 2 — if x > 7, you must walk back across the whole segment plus the overshoot twice: (x - 3) + (x - 7) = 2x - 10, which equals 4 only at x = 7, already counted as an endpoint.
Step 3 — if x < 3, symmetrically (3 - x) + (7 - x) = 10 - 2x, which equals 4 only at x = 3, again an endpoint.
So the solution set is exactly the closed interval 3 <= x <= 7. This is the equality case of the triangle inequality |a| + |b| >= |a + b|, with a = x - 3 and b = 7 - x: equality holds precisely when a and b have the same sign.
Answer: 3 <= x <= 7.
easy.trap: Choosing A, x = 5. The midpoint does satisfy the equation, but so does every other point of the segment, and the question asks what MUST be true - x = 5 is not forced. Choice B keeps only the endpoints, discarding the interior where the equality also holds; choice D has the geometry exactly backwards, since outside the segment the total distance EXCEEDS 4.

easy.question: N is a three-digit positive integer and M is the integer formed by writing the digits of N in reverse order. If N - M = 297 and the digits of N sum to 18, how many possible values of N are there?
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — let N have hundreds digit a, tens digit b and units digit c, so N = 100a + 10b + c and M = 100c + 10b + a.
Step 2 — subtract: N - M = 99a - 99c = 99(a - c). The tens digit cancels.
Step 3 — set 99(a - c) = 297, so a - c = 3.
Step 4 — use the digit sum: a + b + c = 18. Substituting a = c + 3 gives (c + 3) + b + c = 18, so b = 15 - 2c.
Step 5 — impose the digit ranges. b = 15 - 2c must be from 0 to 9, so 2c >= 6, that is c >= 3. Also a = c + 3 must be at most 9, so c <= 6.
Step 6 — c = 3, 4, 5, 6 give b = 9, 7, 5, 3 and a = 6, 7, 8, 9: the integers 693, 774, 855 and 936. That is 4 values.
Check one: 936 - 639 = 297, and 9 + 3 + 6 = 18. Check another: 693 - 396 = 297, and 6 + 9 + 3 = 18. Correct.
Answer: 4.
easy.trap: Stopping at c >= 3 without also imposing a = c + 3 <= 9, which lets c run from 3 to 7 and gives 5 values - the fifth, c = 7, would need a = 10. Answering 3 is the other live error: dividing 297 by 99 to get a - c = 3 and reporting that difference instead of counting the integers.

easy.question: In 2022 a city had 40,000 households, 20 percent of which owned an electric vehicle. From 2022 to 2025 the number of households in the city rose by 25 percent, and the percent of households owning an electric vehicle was 5 percentage points higher in 2025 than in 2022. By what percent did the NUMBER of households owning an electric vehicle increase from 2022 to 2025?
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — Build the 2025 figures before comparing anything. Households in 2025 = 40000 * 1.25 = 50,000.
Step 2 — "5 percentage points higher" adds to the share itself: 20 + 5 = 25 percent of households own one in 2025.
Step 3 — Convert both shares into counts, because the question asks about the number of households, not the share.
Step 4 — 2022: 0.20 * 40000 = 8,000 households own an electric vehicle.
Step 5 — 2025: 0.25 * 50000 = 12,500 households own one.
Step 6 — Increase = 12500 - 8000 = 4,500.
Step 7 — Percent increase = 4500 / 8000 = 0.5625 = 56.25 percent, measured against the ORIGINAL count.
Faster route: the count is households times share, so the count multiplier is 1.25 * (25/20) = 1.25 * 1.25 = 1.5625, a rise of 56.25 percent.
Check: 8000 * 1.5625 = 12,500. Correct.
Answer: C.
easy.trap: Choice B, 36 percent, divides the increase by the NEW count, 4500/12500; a percent increase is always measured against the original. Choice A is where two separate errors land: reading the 5-point move as a 5/20 = 25 percent rise in the count, or reporting the 25 percent household growth as the answer and ignoring the share. Choices D and E are one omission at two levels — E reports the ratio of the counts, 12500/8000 = 156.25 percent, as the change, and D reports the ratio of the shares, 25/20 = 125 percent, the same way; both forget to subtract 1.

easy.question:
Circle C and square S have the same perimeter. Which of the following statements must be true?

Indicate all such statements.
options: A. The area enclosed by C is greater than the area enclosed by S.
B. The ratio of the area enclosed by C to the area enclosed by S is 4/pi.
C. The area enclosed by C is more than 25 percent greater than the area enclosed by S.
D. The area enclosed by C is exactly twice the area enclosed by S.
E. The two enclosed areas are equal.
F. The ratio of the area enclosed by C to the area enclosed by S is pi/4.
easy.explanation: Call the common perimeter p. For the circle, 2*pi*r = p gives r = p/(2*pi), so its area is pi*r^2 = p^2/(4*pi). For the square, the side is p/4, so its area is p^2/16. Dividing, the ratio of circle area to square area is 16/(4*pi) = 4/pi, which is about 1.273. That makes B true and F false, since pi/4 is the reciprocal and is less than 1. A ratio above 1 makes A true, and 1.273 means the circle encloses about 27.3 percent more area, so C is true while D and E are false.
easy.trap: Students reach for pi/4, the familiar ratio of a circle's area to the area of the square that circumscribes it, and endorse F. That ratio applies when the square's side equals the circle's diameter, not when the two figures share a perimeter; with equal perimeters the circle is the larger region, so the ratio must exceed 1.

easy.question: A circle is circumscribed around a right triangle with legs 6 and 8. What is the area of the region inside the circle but outside the triangle?
easy.explanation: For a right triangle, the circumscribed circle has its diameter equal to the hypotenuse. Hypotenuse = √(6²+8²) = √100 = 10. Circumradius = 5. Circle area = π(25) = 25π. Triangle area = (1/2)(6)(8) = 24. Area inside circle but outside triangle = 25π − 24.
easy.trap: Using radius = hypotenuse = 10 instead of radius = hypotenuse/2 = 5, giving circle area = 100π.

easy.question: In the 4-digit number 3d4e, d and e are single digits (the digits are 3, d, 4, e from left to right). What is the greatest value of 3d4e that is divisible by 44?
easy.explanation:
Step 1 — split 44 into COPRIME factors: 44 = 4 x 11. Both tests must pass.
Step 2 — the 4-test reads the last two digits, 4e, that is 40 + e. Since 40 is a multiple of 4, we need e divisible by 4: e = 0, 4 or 8.
Step 3 — the 11-test. Positions from the right: e is 1st, 4 is 2nd, d is 3rd, 3 is 4th. Alternating sum = (e + d) - (4 + 3) = d + e - 7. This must be 0 or a multiple of 11. With d and e digits, d + e runs from 0 to 18, so d + e - 7 runs from -7 to 11. The multiples of 11 available are 0 and 11, giving d + e = 7 or d + e = 18.
Step 4 — combine with the three allowed values of e, and prefer the largest d since d is the more significant digit.
d + e = 18 forces d = e = 9, but e = 9 is not one of 0, 4, 8. Rejected.
d + e = 7 with e = 0 gives d = 7: the number 3,740.
d + e = 7 with e = 4 gives d = 3: the number 3,344.
d + e = 7 with e = 8 would give d = -1, impossible.
Step 5 — the two valid numbers are 3,740 and 3,344. The greater is 3,740.
Check: 3,740/44 = 85, and 3,344/44 = 76. Both exact, and 3,740 > 3,344.
Answer: 3740.
easy.trap: Splitting 44 as 2 x 22 and testing only 'even' plus 'divisible by 22'. Those factors are not coprime, so the pair is not equivalent to 44. The commoner error is finding one valid number and stopping: a student who lands on 3,344 first answers 3344, missing that d = 7, e = 0 also works and is larger. The stem asks for the GREATEST value, so every allowed e must be checked. Answering 2 - the count of valid numbers rather than the number itself - is the third live error.

easy.question: What is the tens digit of (4^30)(5^57)?
easy.explanation: Rewrite everything in terms of primes so the factors of 10 become visible. 4^30 = (2^2)^30 = 2^60, so the product is 2^60 x 5^57. Pair off 57 twos with the 57 fives: 2^57 x 5^57 = 10^57, leaving 2^3 = 8 unpaired. So the product equals 8 x 10^57, which is the digit 8 followed by 57 zeros. Every digit after the leading 8 is a zero, so the tens digit is 0.
easy.trap: Students see a factor of 5 raised to a large power and assume the number ends in 25 or 75, answering 2 or 5. Others notice the leftover 8 and report it as the tens digit. The leftover factor becomes the leading digit, not a trailing one, because all 57 pairs of 2 and 5 push it to the front of a long block of zeros.

medium.question: N is a positive integer and the sum of the digits of N is 45. Which of the following must be true? Select all that apply.
options: E. N has at least 5 digits
medium.explanation:
A. Digit sum 45 = 9 x 5 is a multiple of 9, so 9 divides N. TRUE.
B. 45 is also a multiple of 3, so 3 divides N. (It also follows from A, since 3 divides 9.) TRUE.
C. 45 = 9 x 5, and 9 and 5 are coprime, so divisibility by 45 needs the 5-test too - the last digit must be 0 or 5. N = 99,999 has digit sum 45 but ends in 9, and 99,999/45 = 2,222.2. FALSE.
D. N = 99,990 has digit sum 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 0 = 45 and is even. FALSE.
E. Each digit is at most 9, so k digits give a digit sum of at most 9k. To reach 45 we need 9k >= 45, i.e. k >= 5. TRUE, and 99,999 shows 5 digits is attainable.
Answer: A, B and E.
medium.trap: Selecting C by reading the digit-sum rule as if it extended to any divisor: digit sums decide 3 and 9 and nothing else, so 45 needs a separate 5-test that 99,999 fails. Selecting D comes from noticing that 45 is odd and transferring that parity to N; the digit sum's parity says nothing about the number's, as 99,990 shows.

medium.question:
m^4 / n^8 = 1/16, where n is not 0.
Quantity A: 2m
Quantity B: n^2
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation:
Rewrite the equation as (m / n^2)^4 = 1/16.
A fourth power equals 1/16 for two real values of the base: m / n^2 = 1/2 or m / n^2 = -1/2.
So m = n^2/2 or m = -n^2/2, which means 2m = n^2 or 2m = -n^2.
Case 1: m = 1/2, n = 1 satisfies the equation (m^4/n^8 = 1/16), and then Quantity A = 1 and Quantity B = 1, so they are equal.
Case 2: m = -1/2, n = 1 also satisfies it, and then Quantity A = -1 and Quantity B = 1, so Quantity B is greater.
The comparison depends on the sign of m, which the problem does not give, so the answer is D.
medium.trap: Taking the 4th root as if it gave only the positive value (the habit that works for odd roots such as a cube root), so 2m = n^2 and the quantities are equal (choice C).

medium.question:
A regular polygon has n sides, n an integer, and every one of its interior angles is strictly between 140 and 150 degrees.
Quantity A: The measure, in degrees, of one exterior angle of the polygon
Quantity B: 34
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation:
Interior angle = 180 - 360/n.
140 < 180 - 360/n gives 360/n < 40, so n > 9.
180 - 360/n < 150 gives 360/n > 30, so n < 12.
So n = 10 or n = 11 (n = 9 gives exactly 140 and n = 12 gives exactly 150, both excluded).
Exterior angle = 360/n: n = 10 gives 36, which is more than 34; n = 11 gives about 32.7, which is less than 34.
The comparison flips, so it cannot be determined.
medium.trap: Using only n = 10 (the first integer above 9) gives exterior 36 and choice A.

medium.question: For which of the following values of n is n^3 - n divisible by 12? Select all that apply.
medium.explanation:
Step 1 - factor: n^3 - n = n(n^2 - 1) = (n - 1)n(n + 1), the product of three consecutive integers.
Step 2 - among three consecutive integers one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even, so 6 divides the product for every n. Split 12 into COPRIME factors: 12 = 3 x 4. The 3 is already guaranteed, so everything turns on 4.
Step 3 - if n is odd, n - 1 and n + 1 are consecutive even numbers and one of them is a multiple of 4, so the product carries 4 automatically. If n is even, n - 1 and n + 1 are both odd and the only even factor is n itself, so 4 divides the product only when 4 divides n.
A. n = 2: 1 x 2 x 3 = 6, and 6/12 is not an integer. n is even and 4 does not divide 2. FALSE.
B. n = 3: 2 x 3 x 4 = 24 = 12 x 2. TRUE.
C. n = 5: 4 x 5 x 6 = 120 = 12 x 10. TRUE.
D. n = 6: 5 x 6 x 7 = 210, and 210/12 = 17.5. n is even and 4 does not divide 6. FALSE.
E. n = 8: 7 x 8 x 9 = 504 = 12 x 42. n is even, but 4 divides 8, so the factor of 4 arrives anyway. TRUE.
Check: the rule is 'every odd n works, and an even n works exactly when 4 divides n'. The even values offered are 2, 6 and 8; 4 divides only 8, and 8 is the only even one selected.
Answer: B, C and E.
medium.trap: Stopping at Step 2 and selecting all five on the correct but insufficient fact that three consecutive integers are always divisible by 6. Twelve needs a second factor of 2: n = 2 gives 6 and n = 6 gives 210, and 12 divides neither. The opposite error is reading Step 3 as 'n must be odd' and selecting only B and C, dropping E; n = 8 supplies the factor of 4 by itself.

medium.question: The function f satisfies f(x) + f(x + 1) = 2x + 3 for all real x. If f(1) = 2, what is f(3)?
medium.trap: Students substitute x=3 into the equation and compute f(3)+f(4) = 9, then incorrectly set f(3) = 9 without knowing f(4).

medium.question: How many 4-letter strings can be formed from the letters A, B, C, D, and E if no letter is used more than once and the string does not contain both A and B?
medium.explanation:
Total codewords (no restriction): P(5,4) = 5×4×3×2 = 120.
Invalid codewords (contain both A and B): Choose 2 positions from 4 for A and B, then arrange A and B in those positions: P(4,2) = 4×3 = 12 ways. Fill the remaining 2 positions from {C,D,E}: P(3,2) = 3×2 = 6 ways.
Invalid = 12 × 6 = 72.
Valid = 120 - 72 = 48.
medium.trap: Students use combinations instead of permutations for codewords (since order matters in coding strings), computing C(5,4)=5 instead of P(5,4)=120.

medium.question: If j and m are each positive integers between 10 and 40, then (4 + j)/(9 + m) will be equal to 4/9 for how many pairs (j, m)?
medium.explanation: Cross-multiplying gives 9(4 + j) = 4(9 + m), so 36 + 9j = 36 + 4m and therefore 9j = 4m. That forces j/m = 4/9, so j = 4t and m = 9t for some positive integer t. For j to lie strictly between 10 and 40, t must run from 3 to 9. For m = 9t to lie strictly between 10 and 40, t must be 2, 3 or 4. Only t = 3 and t = 4 satisfy both, giving the pairs (12, 27) and (16, 36).
medium.trap: Students derive 9j = 4m and then count every multiple of 4 that j could be, arriving at seven, without checking that the matching m = 9j/4 also falls between 10 and 40. The range on the second variable is the binding constraint.

medium.question:
The circle graph shows how Fenwick Municipal Library allocated its 2024 operating budget of $1,500,000 among five categories, and the table below it gives the amount, in dollars, that each category received in 2023.

Quantity A: Facilities' 2024 allocation as a percent of the library's total 2024 budget
Quantity B: Facilities' 2023 allocation as a percent of the library's total 2023 budget
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation: Quantity A is read straight off the circle graph: Facilities took 15 percent of the 2024 budget. For Quantity B, the chart prints the 2023 total as $1,280,000 (and the five table entries confirm it), and Facilities received $200,000 of that, so its share is 200,000/1,280,000 = 0.15625, or 15.625 percent. Since 15.625 is greater than 15, Quantity B is greater.
medium.trap: Comparing dollars instead of shares makes Quantity A look bigger: Facilities got 0.15 * 1,500,000 = $225,000 in 2024 against $200,000 in 2023, which points to choice A. A larger dollar amount out of a much larger budget can still be a smaller share of it.

medium.question: How many three-digit positive integers have digits that sum to 4?
medium.explanation:
Step 1 — let the digits be a, b, c with a + b + c = 4 and a at least 1, since a three-digit integer cannot lead with 0.
Step 2 — handle the leading-digit restriction by substitution. Put a = a' + 1, where a' is 0 or more. Then a' + b + c = 3, with every variable from 0 up.
Step 3 — count the non-negative solutions of a' + b + c = 3. They are the ways to place 3 identical units into 3 slots: C(3 + 2, 2) = C(5, 2) = 10. No digit can exceed 9 here, so no solution has to be thrown out.
Step 4 — so there are 10 such integers. Listing them confirms it: 103, 112, 121, 130, 202, 211, 220, 301, 310, 400.
Check: that list has 10 entries and every one has digit sum 4.
Answer: C.
medium.trap: Answering 15, choice E - the count of non-negative solutions of a + b + c = 4, which is C(6, 2) = 15. That count includes the five with a = 0 (004, 013, 022, 031, 040), and those are not three-digit integers. Choice D, 13, comes from discarding only 004 and 040, which obviously are not three-digit, while keeping 013, 031 and 022. Choice B, 4, counts the digit multisets {4,0,0}, {3,1,0}, {2,2,0}, {2,1,1} rather than the integers they arrange into. Choice A, 3, comes from requiring every digit to be non-zero, leaving only 112, 121 and 211.

medium.question: The sequence b(1), b(2), b(3), ... is defined by b(1) = 3, b(2) = 2, and b(n) = b(n - 1) x b(n - 2) for every integer n greater than 2. What is the value of b(7)?
medium.explanation: Build the terms in factored form so the exponents stay visible. b(1) = 3 = (2^0)(3^1) and b(2) = 2 = (2^1)(3^0). Multiplying consecutive terms adds exponents, so b(3) = 6 = (2^1)(3^1), b(4) = b(3)b(2) = (2^2)(3^1), b(5) = b(4)b(3) = (2^3)(3^2), b(6) = b(5)b(4) = (2^5)(3^3), and b(7) = b(6)b(5) = (2^8)(3^5). As a check, (2^8)(3^5) = 256 x 243 = 62,208, which is indeed 864 x 72.
medium.trap: Students carry the recursion one step too far and answer (2^13)(3^8), which is b(8), not b(7). Others multiply only the most recent term by the first term instead of by the term before it, producing (2^5)(3^5). Tracking the exponents of 2 and of 3 as two separate Fibonacci-style chains keeps the bookkeeping honest.

medium.question: A tank holds a mixture of liquids A, B and C in the ratio 3:4:5. Then 8 liters of A are removed and 8 liters of C are added, after which the ratio of A to B to C is 1:4:7. What was the original total volume of the mixture, in liters?
medium.explanation:
Step 1 — name k. A = 3k, B = 4k, C = 5k, and the total is 12k.
Step 2 — name the invariant. Exactly 8 liters left and exactly 8 liters came back, so the TOTAL never moved. It is 12k before and after. B never moved either.
Step 3 — use the invariant. The new ratio 1:4:7 has 1 + 4 + 7 = 12 parts, and those 12 parts still add to 12k, so one new part is worth exactly k. (This is the whole trick: the same total split into the same number of parts means the part size is unchanged.)
Step 4 — B confirms it: B is 4 new parts = 4k, and B did not change. Consistent.
Step 5 — A is now 1 new part = k, and A is also 3k - 8:
3k - 8 = k
2k = 8
k = 4
Step 6 — original total = 12k = 12 x 4 = 48 liters.
Check: start 12, 16, 20 (total 48). After: 4, 16, 28 (total 48), and 4:16:28 = 1:4:7. Correct.
Answer: 48.
medium.trap: Answering 4 (the value of k) or 12 (the original volume of A) instead of the total. The setup error is subtracting 8 from the total as well - it is an exchange, so the total is invariant, and noticing that is what collapses the three-part algebra into the single equation 3k - 8 = k.

medium.question:
m < 0 and n is not equal to 0
Quantity A: |n^4 + m|
Quantity B: |m - n^4|
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation: Since n is nonzero and 4 is even, n^4 is a strictly positive number. Since m is negative, write |m| = -m, a positive number. Now handle each column. In Quantity B, m - n^4 is a negative number minus a positive number, so it is negative, and removing the bars flips the sign: |m - n^4| = n^4 - m = n^4 + |m|. That is the sum of two positive quantities. In Quantity A, n^4 + m = n^4 - |m|, so Quantity A = |n^4 - |m||, the absolute difference of the same two positive quantities. For any two positive numbers P and Q, |P - Q| is strictly less than P + Q. Therefore Quantity A is always less than Quantity B.
medium.trap: Testing one convenient case such as m = -1 and n = 1, getting Quantity A = 0 and Quantity B = 2, and then answering D because absolute values feel unpredictable. The two columns are structurally the difference and the sum of the same pair of positive numbers, so the sum always wins no matter what m and n are.

medium.question:
In triangle PQR, PQ = 5, QR = 12, and PR = 12.5.
Quantity A: The measure of angle Q, in degrees
Quantity B: The sum of the measures of angles P and R, in degrees
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
medium.explanation:
1. The angles of a triangle sum to 180, so Quantity B = 180 - (measure of angle Q).
2. So Quantity A < Quantity B exactly when angle Q < 90.
3. Angle Q lies opposite the longest side PR = 12.5. Compare PQ^2 + QR^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 with PR^2 = 156.25.
4. Since 169 > 156.25, the side opposite Q is shorter than it would be in a right triangle, so the angle opposite PR is acute: Q < 90.
5. Therefore Q < 180 - Q, so Quantity B is greater.
Check: with legs 5 and 12, a right angle at Q would need PR = 13. Shortening PR to 12.5 closes the angle at Q, so Q is less than 90 and P + R is more than 90.
medium.trap: Noticing the 5 and 12 sides and assuming a 5-12-13 right triangle gives Q = 90 and P + R = 90, so the quantities look equal (choice C).

medium.question: A trader's profit on item X is 20 percent of the selling price of X, and his profit on item Y is 20 percent of the cost price of Y. The two items have the same selling price, and his total profit on the two items together is $330. By how many dollars does the cost price of Y exceed the cost price of X?
medium.explanation:
Step 1 — call the common selling price S and express each profit in terms of S.
Step 2 — item X: profit = 0.20*S directly, since X's profit is a percent of its own selling price. So X's cost is 0.80*S.
Step 3 — item Y: profit = 0.20*CP(Y) and SP = 1.20*CP(Y) = S, so CP(Y) = S/1.20 and the profit is 0.20*S/1.20 = S/6.
Step 4 — add the profits: 0.20*S + S/6 = S/5 + S/6 = 11S/30 = 330, so S = 330*30/11 = $900.
Step 5 — the two cost prices: CP(X) = 0.80*900 = $720 and CP(Y) = 900/1.20 = $750.
Step 6 — CP(Y) - CP(X) = 750 - 720 = $30.
Check the profits: X makes 900 - 720 = $180, and 180/900 = 0.20 of X's selling price; Y makes 900 - 750 = $150, and 150/750 = 0.20 of Y's cost. Together 180 + 150 = $330, as given. Correct.
Answer: 30.
medium.trap: Splitting the $330 evenly, $165 each, which would force the two costs to be equal and give an answer of 0. The two rules do not share a base, so at a common selling price the item priced on its selling price earns MORE (20 percent of S) than the item priced on its cost (S/6, about 16.67 percent of S), and the profits must split 180 to 150. The other slip is reading 'the same selling price' as 'the same cost price' and concluding that the selling prices differ instead.

medium.question: A circle of radius r is rolled inside a circle of radius 4r without slipping. If the small circle starts with its center at distance 3r from the big circle's center, and completes one full trip around the interior of the big circle, how many complete rotations does the small circle make about its own center?
medium.explanation: When a circle of radius r rolls inside a circle of radius R, the small circle's center travels on a circle of radius R − r = 4r − r = 3r. The path length of the small circle's center = 2π(3r). Each full rotation of the small circle covers a distance of 2πr (its circumference). Number of rotations = 2π(3r) / (2πr) = 3. The small circle makes 3 complete rotations.
medium.trap: Using R = 4r as the path radius instead of R − r = 3r, and getting 2π(4r)/(2πr) = 4 rotations.

hard.question: Let P be the product of all 60 numbers of the form (m + 2)/m, where m is an integer and 1 <= m <= 60. What is the value of P?
hard.explanation: Write the product out as one big fraction. The numerators run 3, 4, 5, ..., 62 and the denominators run 1, 2, 3, ..., 60. Every integer from 3 through 60 appears once on top and once on the bottom, so all of those cancel. What survives on top is 61 x 62 and what survives on the bottom is 1 x 2. Therefore P = (61 x 62)/2 = 3,782/2 = 1,891.
hard.trap: Students cancel correctly on top but forget that two denominators, the 1 and the 2, are left behind, and answer 3,782. Others treat the product as telescoping one step at a time and stop at 62/1, answering 62. Because each numerator is two ahead of its denominator, exactly two terms survive at each end, not one.

hard.question: A sphere is inscribed in a cube (touches all 6 faces). A second sphere is circumscribed about the same cube (passes through all 8 vertices). What is the ratio of the volume of the circumscribed sphere to the volume of the inscribed sphere?
hard.explanation: Let the cube have side s. Inscribed sphere: diameter = s, so r₁ = s/2. Circumscribed sphere: diameter = space diagonal = s√3, so r₂ = s√3/2. Volume ratio = (r₂/r₁)³ = (s√3/2 ÷ s/2)³ = (√3)³ = 3√3.
hard.trap: Students compute the ratio of radii (r₂/r₁ = √3) and report √3 as the volume ratio. Volume scales as r³, so the ratio of volumes is (√3)³ = 3√3 ≈ 5.196, not √3 ≈ 1.732.

hard.question:
In the xy-plane, circle C is the graph of x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y = 0.
Quantity A: the radius of circle C
Quantity B: the distance from the center of circle C to the point (7, -1)
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation: Complete the square in each variable: x^2 - 6x becomes (x - 3)^2 - 9 and y^2 + 8y becomes (y + 4)^2 - 16. The equation turns into (x - 3)^2 + (y + 4)^2 - 25 = 0, that is (x - 3)^2 + (y + 4)^2 = 25. So the center is (3, -4) and the radius is 5. The distance from (3, -4) to (7, -1) has horizontal part 4 and vertical part 3, giving sqrt(16 + 9) = 5. The two quantities match.
hard.trap: The 0 on the right-hand side invites students to conclude the radius is 0 and pick B. Completing the square shifts 9 and 16 across to the right, so r^2 = 25 and r = 5 — and the point (7, -1) turns out to sit on the circle itself.

hard.question:
Suppose y = 3x - 8 and x exceeds 3.
Quantity A: How much larger y becomes, as a percent of its original value, after x is raised by 25 percent
Quantity B: 25%
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation:
Because x > 3, the original y = 3x - 8 is positive (it is greater than 1), so a percent increase is well defined.
Raising x by 25% makes the new x equal to 1.25x, so the new y = 3(1.25x) - 8 = 3.75x - 8.
The increase in y is (3.75x - 8) - (3x - 8) = 0.75x.
Percent increase = 0.75x / (3x - 8). Compare with 25% = 0.75x / (3x).
The denominator 3x - 8 is positive but smaller than 3x, so 0.75x / (3x - 8) > 0.75x / (3x) = 0.25.
Quantity A is greater.
Tests: x = 5 gives y = 7 and new y = 10.75, an increase of 3.75/7 = 53.6%; x = 100 gives y = 292 and an increase of 75/292 = 25.7%. Both exceed 25%, and the gap never closes.
hard.trap: Assuming that a linear function must change by the same percent as its input, so the quantities are equal (choice C). That is only true when the constant term is zero; here the constant -8 shrinks y and makes the percent change bigger.

hard.question:
n is an integer.
Quantity A: (1/4)^n
Quantity B: (1/5)^n
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation:
If n = 0: both quantities equal 1, so they're equal.
If n is a positive integer (e.g., n = 1): (1/4) = 0.25 > (1/5) = 0.2, so Quantity A is greater; this pattern holds for all positive n since 1/4 > 1/5.
If n is a negative integer (e.g., n = -1): (1/4)^-1 = 4 and (1/5)^-1 = 5, so Quantity B (5) is greater than Quantity A (4).
Since the outcome depends on whether n is positive, negative, or zero, the relationship cannot be determined.
hard.trap: Students assume n is a positive integer (the 'default' case) and conclude Quantity A is always greater, without testing n = 0 or negative n.

hard.question: A list contains 21 different numbers. The 10 numbers that are larger than the middle value of the list have a mean of 80, and the 10 numbers that are smaller than the middle value have a mean of 40. The mean of all 21 numbers is a whole number. What is the middle value of the list?
hard.explanation:
Let m be the middle value (the median). Total = 10*80 + 10*40 + m = 1200 + m.
The mean (1200 + m)/21 is an integer, so 1200 + m is a multiple of 21.
1200 = 21*57 + 3, so m must leave remainder 18 when divided by 21: m = 18, 39, 60, 81, ...
The 10 numbers above m average 80, so m < 80; the 10 numbers below m average 40, so m > 40.
Only 60 lies strictly between 40 and 80.
Check: (1200 + 60)/21 = 60; the lists can be filled in with distinct values, for example below m averaging 40 and above m averaging 80.
hard.trap: Using only the divisibility condition and picking the first candidate m = 18 (or 39 or 81), which lies outside the range forced by the two group means.

hard.question: For any real number x, ⌊x⌋ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to x. If x is a real number and n is an integer, which of the following must be true?
hard.explanation:
A: write x = ⌊x⌋ + f with 0 ≤ f < 1. Then x + n = (⌊x⌋ + n) + f, where ⌊x⌋ + n is an integer and f is still less than 1, so ⌊x + n⌋ = ⌊x⌋ + n. True for every real x and every integer n. Check on a negative: x = −2.4, n = 5 gives ⌊2.6⌋ = 2 and ⌊−2.4⌋ + 5 = −3 + 5 = 2.
B: x = 0.5 gives ⌊0.5⌋ + ⌊−0.5⌋ = 0 + (−1) = −1, not 0.
C: x = 0.5, n = 2 gives ⌊1⌋ = 1 but 2⌊0.5⌋ = 0.
D: x = 2.7 gives ⌊2.7⌋ = 2, and 2 ≥ 2.7 is false; the inequality runs the other way.
E: x = 1.5 gives ⌊2.25⌋ = 2 but ⌊1.5⌋² = 1.
So A.
hard.trap: Students pick D from a half-remembered rule that the floor 'rounds x to an integer', losing the direction of the inequality; in fact ⌊x⌋ ≤ x. Option C tempts anyone who treats the floor as linear, but ⌊2 × 0.5⌋ = 1 while 2⌊0.5⌋ = 0. Only a shift by an integer, as in A, commutes with the floor.

hard.question: Events A and B satisfy P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, and P(A and B) = 0.2. Which of the following statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: C. P(A occurs but B does not) = 0.3
D. P(exactly one of A and B occurs) = 0.7
hard.explanation:
Build the four regions from the given numbers first.
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) = 0.5 + 0.4 - 0.2 = 0.7.
A only = 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.3. B only = 0.4 - 0.2 = 0.2. Both = 0.2. Neither = 1 - 0.7 = 0.3.
Check: 0.3 + 0.2 + 0.2 + 0.3 = 1.0.
A - the union is 0.7. TRUE.
B - 'neither' is the complement of the union: 1 - 0.7 = 0.3, not 0.1. FALSE.
C - A but not B = 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.3. TRUE.
D - exactly one = (A only) + (B only) = 0.3 + 0.2 = 0.5, not 0.7. The value 0.7 is 'at least one'. FALSE.
E - P(not B) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6. TRUE.
Answer: A, C, E.
hard.trap: B is the value 1 - P(A) - P(B) = 0.1, which subtracts the 0.2 overlap twice and never adds it back. D confuses 'exactly one' with 'at least one': the union 0.7 includes the 0.2 who get both, so exactly one is 0.7 - 0.2 = 0.5.

hard.question: Two cylinders are formed from the same rectangular sheet (6 × 10): Cylinder P rolls along the 6-cm edge (6 cm becomes height), and Cylinder Q rolls along the 10-cm edge (10 cm becomes height). What is the ratio Volume(P) / Volume(Q)?
hard.explanation: Cylinder P: height = 6, circumference = 10 → 2πr_P = 10 → r_P = 5/π. V(P) = π(5/π)²(6) = π(25/π²)(6) = 150/π. Cylinder Q: height = 10, circumference = 6 → 2πr_Q = 6 → r_Q = 3/π. V(Q) = π(9/π²)(10) = 90/π. Ratio V(P)/V(Q) = (150/π)/(90/π) = 150/90 = 5/3.
hard.trap: Students square only the radius ratio, (5/3)^2 = 25/9 (E), forgetting the heights differ; or they invert the ratio and choose 3/5 (B).

hard.question:
The integers m and n satisfy m^2 + n^2 = 130.

Which of the following values mn can take?

Indicate all such values.
hard.explanation:
Find every way to write 130 as a sum of two perfect squares.
130 - 1 = 129, 130 - 4 = 126, 130 - 9 = 121 = 11^2, 130 - 16 = 114, 130 - 25 = 105, 130 - 36 = 94, 130 - 49 = 81 = 9^2, 130 - 64 = 66, 130 - 81 = 49, 130 - 100 = 30, 130 - 121 = 9. So the only unordered pairs of absolute values are {11, 3} and {9, 7}.
With signs allowed, mn = +-(11*3) = +-33 or +-(9*7) = +-63.
A (-77): would need 11 and 7, but 121 + 49 = 170. FALSE.
B (-63): m = 9, n = -7. TRUE.
C (-33): m = 11, n = -3. TRUE.
D (0): needs m = 0 or n = 0, so the other would satisfy a^2 = 130, which is not a square. FALSE.
E (21): would need 3 and 7, but 9 + 49 = 58. FALSE.
F (33): m = 11, n = 3. TRUE.
G (63): m = 9, n = 7. TRUE.
H (77): same as A, FALSE.
Answer: B, C, F, G.
hard.trap: Multiplying numbers from different pairs, such as 11*7 = 77 (A, H) or 3*7 = 21 (E), instead of the two that actually pair up; or forgetting negative signs and picking only the positive products.

hard.question: For each integer k from 1 through 50, form the fraction (k+2)/k. What is the product of all 50 of these fractions?
hard.explanation:
Write out the product: (3/1) * (4/2) * (5/3) * ... * (51/49) * (52/50).
Numerators are 3, 4, ..., 52; denominators are 1, 2, ..., 50.
Every number from 3 to 50 appears in both, so those cancel. Left in the numerator: 51 and 52. Left in the denominator: 1 and 2.
Product = (51 * 52)/(1 * 2) = 2652/2 = 1326.
Check on a short version, k = 1 to 3: (3/1)(4/2)(5/3) = 10, and the pattern (4 * 5)/(1 * 2) = 10.
hard.trap: Forgetting the leftover denominators 1 and 2, and answering 51 * 52 = 2652; or expecting only the last numerator to survive as in (k+1)/k products, giving 52.

hard.question: A large cube is assembled from 64 identical small cubes arranged 4 by 4 by 4. Exactly 12 of the small cubes are white and the other 52 are red. What is the least possible fraction of the large cube's surface area that is red?
hard.explanation:
The large cube's surface has 6 * 16 = 96 small faces.
Small cubes by exposed faces: 8 corner cubes show 3 faces each (24); 24 edge cubes show 2 faces each (48); 24 face cubes show 1 face each (24); 8 interior cubes show 0. Total 24 + 48 + 24 = 96.
To minimize red area, the white cubes should show as many faces as possible: 8 corners (24 faces) plus 4 edge cubes (8 faces) = 12 cubes showing 32 faces.
Red faces = 96 - 32 = 64.
Fraction = 64/96 = 2/3.
Check: swapping any white cube for a cube with fewer exposed faces only lowers white exposure.
hard.trap: Using only the 8 corners for white and forgetting the other 4 white cubes also show faces gives 72/96 = 3/4 (choice D); assuming all 12 white cubes show 3 faces gives 60/96 = 5/8 (choice A); hiding the white cubes (the greatest fraction instead of the least) gives 23/24 (choice E).

hard.question:
ABCD is a square. Point E lies outside the square, on the opposite side of line CD from A and B, with DE = DC and angle CDE = 40 degrees. Segment AE is drawn.
Quantity A: The measure, in degrees, of angle AED
Quantity B: 30
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation:
DA = DC because ABCD is a square, and DE = DC is given, so DA = DE and triangle ADE is isosceles with its apex at D.
Angle ADE = angle ADC + angle CDE = 90 + 40 = 130 degrees (E is on the far side of DC from A, so the angles add).
The base angles are equal: angle AED = (180 - 130)/2 = 25 degrees.
Quantity A = 25 < 30 = Quantity B.
Check: angles of triangle ADE = 130 + 25 + 25 = 180.
hard.trap: Forgetting that DA = DE and using the full 180 - 130 = 50 for angle AED gives 50, which exceeds 30 (choice A).

hard.question:
x and y are real numbers, and x + y > 6.
Quantity A: The average of x^2 and y^2
Quantity B: 9
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
hard.explanation:
1. For any real numbers, (x - y)^2 >= 0, which expands to x^2 + y^2 >= 2xy.
2. Then 2(x^2 + y^2) >= x^2 + y^2 + 2xy = (x + y)^2, so (x^2 + y^2)/2 >= (x + y)^2 / 4.
3. Because x + y > 6, which is positive, (x + y)^2 > 36, so (x^2 + y^2)/2 > 9 for every allowed pair.
4. Test values: x = 3.1, y = 3 gives 9.31; x = 7, y = 0 gives 24.5; x = 10, y = -3.5 gives 56.125; x = -2, y = 8.5 gives 38.125. All exceed 9.
5. The boundary case x = y = 3 would give exactly 9 but is excluded by the strict inequality. Quantity A is always greater.
hard.trap: Substituting the boundary x = y = 3, which gives exactly 9, and concluding that the quantities are equal (choice C), even though x + y > 6 rules that pair out and pushes the average of the squares above 9.

hard.question:
A variable is normally distributed with mean m and standard deviation s. Define three regions:
Region I: values more than 2 SDs below the mean
Region II: values between 1 and 2 SDs above the mean
Region III: values more than 3 SDs above the mean
Using the 68-95-99.7 rule, approximately what percent of the values lie in NONE of these three regions?
hard.explanation:
Compute each region separately, halving every band because the curve is symmetric.
Step 1 - Region I, below m - 2s. About 95% lies within 2 SDs, so 5% lies outside, and half of that is in the lower tail: 2.5%.
Step 2 - Region II, between m + s and m + 2s. Within 2 SDs is 95% and within 1 SD is 68%, so the two 2nd-SD bands hold 95 - 68 = 27% between them, and one of them holds 13.5%.
Step 3 - Region III, above m + 3s. About 99.7% lies within 3 SDs, so 0.3% lies outside, and half of that is in the upper tail: 0.15%.
Step 4 - the three regions do not overlap (Region II stops at 2 SDs, Region III starts at 3 SDs), so add them: 2.5 + 13.5 + 0.15 = 16.15%.
Step 5 - the question asks for everything else: 100 - 16.15 = 83.85%.
Answer: about 83.85%.
hard.trap: Choice A, 16.15%, is the total IN the three regions - the right work stopped one step early. Choice E, 84%, uses 2.35% for Region I, which is the band between 2 and 3 SDs rather than everything beyond 2 SDs. Choice C, 83.7%, forgets to halve the 0.3% outside 3 SDs, and choice B, 81.35%, forgets to halve the 5% outside 2 SDs.

questions.question: N is a positive integer and the sum of the digits of N is 45. Which of the following must be true? Select all that apply.
options: E. N has at least 5 digits
questions.explanation:
A. Digit sum 45 = 9 x 5 is a multiple of 9, so 9 divides N. TRUE.
B. 45 is also a multiple of 3, so 3 divides N. (It also follows from A, since 3 divides 9.) TRUE.
C. 45 = 9 x 5, and 9 and 5 are coprime, so divisibility by 45 needs the 5-test too - the last digit must be 0 or 5. N = 99,999 has digit sum 45 but ends in 9, and 99,999/45 = 2,222.2. FALSE.
D. N = 99,990 has digit sum 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 0 = 45 and is even. FALSE.
E. Each digit is at most 9, so k digits give a digit sum of at most 9k. To reach 45 we need 9k >= 45, i.e. k >= 5. TRUE, and 99,999 shows 5 digits is attainable.
Answer: A, B and E.
questions.trap: Selecting C by reading the digit-sum rule as if it extended to any divisor: digit sums decide 3 and 9 and nothing else, so 45 needs a separate 5-test that 99,999 fails. Selecting D comes from noticing that 45 is odd and transferring that parity to N; the digit sum's parity says nothing about the number's, as 99,990 shows.

questions.question:
m^4 / n^8 = 1/16, where n is not 0.
Quantity A: 2m
Quantity B: n^2
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Rewrite the equation as (m / n^2)^4 = 1/16.
A fourth power equals 1/16 for two real values of the base: m / n^2 = 1/2 or m / n^2 = -1/2.
So m = n^2/2 or m = -n^2/2, which means 2m = n^2 or 2m = -n^2.
Case 1: m = 1/2, n = 1 satisfies the equation (m^4/n^8 = 1/16), and then Quantity A = 1 and Quantity B = 1, so they are equal.
Case 2: m = -1/2, n = 1 also satisfies it, and then Quantity A = -1 and Quantity B = 1, so Quantity B is greater.
The comparison depends on the sign of m, which the problem does not give, so the answer is D.
questions.trap: Taking the 4th root as if it gave only the positive value (the habit that works for odd roots such as a cube root), so 2m = n^2 and the quantities are equal (choice C).

questions.question:
A regular polygon has n sides, n an integer, and every one of its interior angles is strictly between 140 and 150 degrees.
Quantity A: The measure, in degrees, of one exterior angle of the polygon
Quantity B: 34
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
Interior angle = 180 - 360/n.
140 < 180 - 360/n gives 360/n < 40, so n > 9.
180 - 360/n < 150 gives 360/n > 30, so n < 12.
So n = 10 or n = 11 (n = 9 gives exactly 140 and n = 12 gives exactly 150, both excluded).
Exterior angle = 360/n: n = 10 gives 36, which is more than 34; n = 11 gives about 32.7, which is less than 34.
The comparison flips, so it cannot be determined.
questions.trap: Using only n = 10 (the first integer above 9) gives exterior 36 and choice A.

questions.question: For which of the following values of n is n^3 - n divisible by 12? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 - factor: n^3 - n = n(n^2 - 1) = (n - 1)n(n + 1), the product of three consecutive integers.
Step 2 - among three consecutive integers one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even, so 6 divides the product for every n. Split 12 into COPRIME factors: 12 = 3 x 4. The 3 is already guaranteed, so everything turns on 4.
Step 3 - if n is odd, n - 1 and n + 1 are consecutive even numbers and one of them is a multiple of 4, so the product carries 4 automatically. If n is even, n - 1 and n + 1 are both odd and the only even factor is n itself, so 4 divides the product only when 4 divides n.
A. n = 2: 1 x 2 x 3 = 6, and 6/12 is not an integer. n is even and 4 does not divide 2. FALSE.
B. n = 3: 2 x 3 x 4 = 24 = 12 x 2. TRUE.
C. n = 5: 4 x 5 x 6 = 120 = 12 x 10. TRUE.
D. n = 6: 5 x 6 x 7 = 210, and 210/12 = 17.5. n is even and 4 does not divide 6. FALSE.
E. n = 8: 7 x 8 x 9 = 504 = 12 x 42. n is even, but 4 divides 8, so the factor of 4 arrives anyway. TRUE.
Check: the rule is 'every odd n works, and an even n works exactly when 4 divides n'. The even values offered are 2, 6 and 8; 4 divides only 8, and 8 is the only even one selected.
Answer: B, C and E.
questions.trap: Stopping at Step 2 and selecting all five on the correct but insufficient fact that three consecutive integers are always divisible by 6. Twelve needs a second factor of 2: n = 2 gives 6 and n = 6 gives 210, and 12 divides neither. The opposite error is reading Step 3 as 'n must be odd' and selecting only B and C, dropping E; n = 8 supplies the factor of 4 by itself.

questions.question: The function f satisfies f(x) + f(x + 1) = 2x + 3 for all real x. If f(1) = 2, what is f(3)?
questions.trap: Students substitute x=3 into the equation and compute f(3)+f(4) = 9, then incorrectly set f(3) = 9 without knowing f(4).

questions.question: How many 4-letter strings can be formed from the letters A, B, C, D, and E if no letter is used more than once and the string does not contain both A and B?
questions.explanation:
Total codewords (no restriction): P(5,4) = 5×4×3×2 = 120.
Invalid codewords (contain both A and B): Choose 2 positions from 4 for A and B, then arrange A and B in those positions: P(4,2) = 4×3 = 12 ways. Fill the remaining 2 positions from {C,D,E}: P(3,2) = 3×2 = 6 ways.
Invalid = 12 × 6 = 72.
Valid = 120 - 72 = 48.
questions.trap: Students use combinations instead of permutations for codewords (since order matters in coding strings), computing C(5,4)=5 instead of P(5,4)=120.

questions.question: If j and m are each positive integers between 10 and 40, then (4 + j)/(9 + m) will be equal to 4/9 for how many pairs (j, m)?
questions.explanation: Cross-multiplying gives 9(4 + j) = 4(9 + m), so 36 + 9j = 36 + 4m and therefore 9j = 4m. That forces j/m = 4/9, so j = 4t and m = 9t for some positive integer t. For j to lie strictly between 10 and 40, t must run from 3 to 9. For m = 9t to lie strictly between 10 and 40, t must be 2, 3 or 4. Only t = 3 and t = 4 satisfy both, giving the pairs (12, 27) and (16, 36).
questions.trap: Students derive 9j = 4m and then count every multiple of 4 that j could be, arriving at seven, without checking that the matching m = 9j/4 also falls between 10 and 40. The range on the second variable is the binding constraint.

questions.question:
The circle graph shows how Fenwick Municipal Library allocated its 2024 operating budget of $1,500,000 among five categories, and the table below it gives the amount, in dollars, that each category received in 2023.

Quantity A: Facilities' 2024 allocation as a percent of the library's total 2024 budget
Quantity B: Facilities' 2023 allocation as a percent of the library's total 2023 budget
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Quantity A is read straight off the circle graph: Facilities took 15 percent of the 2024 budget. For Quantity B, the chart prints the 2023 total as $1,280,000 (and the five table entries confirm it), and Facilities received $200,000 of that, so its share is 200,000/1,280,000 = 0.15625, or 15.625 percent. Since 15.625 is greater than 15, Quantity B is greater.
questions.trap: Comparing dollars instead of shares makes Quantity A look bigger: Facilities got 0.15 * 1,500,000 = $225,000 in 2024 against $200,000 in 2023, which points to choice A. A larger dollar amount out of a much larger budget can still be a smaller share of it.

questions.question: How many three-digit positive integers have digits that sum to 4?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — let the digits be a, b, c with a + b + c = 4 and a at least 1, since a three-digit integer cannot lead with 0.
Step 2 — handle the leading-digit restriction by substitution. Put a = a' + 1, where a' is 0 or more. Then a' + b + c = 3, with every variable from 0 up.
Step 3 — count the non-negative solutions of a' + b + c = 3. They are the ways to place 3 identical units into 3 slots: C(3 + 2, 2) = C(5, 2) = 10. No digit can exceed 9 here, so no solution has to be thrown out.
Step 4 — so there are 10 such integers. Listing them confirms it: 103, 112, 121, 130, 202, 211, 220, 301, 310, 400.
Check: that list has 10 entries and every one has digit sum 4.
Answer: C.
questions.trap: Answering 15, choice E - the count of non-negative solutions of a + b + c = 4, which is C(6, 2) = 15. That count includes the five with a = 0 (004, 013, 022, 031, 040), and those are not three-digit integers. Choice D, 13, comes from discarding only 004 and 040, which obviously are not three-digit, while keeping 013, 031 and 022. Choice B, 4, counts the digit multisets {4,0,0}, {3,1,0}, {2,2,0}, {2,1,1} rather than the integers they arrange into. Choice A, 3, comes from requiring every digit to be non-zero, leaving only 112, 121 and 211.

questions.question: The sequence b(1), b(2), b(3), ... is defined by b(1) = 3, b(2) = 2, and b(n) = b(n - 1) x b(n - 2) for every integer n greater than 2. What is the value of b(7)?
questions.explanation: Build the terms in factored form so the exponents stay visible. b(1) = 3 = (2^0)(3^1) and b(2) = 2 = (2^1)(3^0). Multiplying consecutive terms adds exponents, so b(3) = 6 = (2^1)(3^1), b(4) = b(3)b(2) = (2^2)(3^1), b(5) = b(4)b(3) = (2^3)(3^2), b(6) = b(5)b(4) = (2^5)(3^3), and b(7) = b(6)b(5) = (2^8)(3^5). As a check, (2^8)(3^5) = 256 x 243 = 62,208, which is indeed 864 x 72.
questions.trap: Students carry the recursion one step too far and answer (2^13)(3^8), which is b(8), not b(7). Others multiply only the most recent term by the first term instead of by the term before it, producing (2^5)(3^5). Tracking the exponents of 2 and of 3 as two separate Fibonacci-style chains keeps the bookkeeping honest.

questions.question: A tank holds a mixture of liquids A, B and C in the ratio 3:4:5. Then 8 liters of A are removed and 8 liters of C are added, after which the ratio of A to B to C is 1:4:7. What was the original total volume of the mixture, in liters?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — name k. A = 3k, B = 4k, C = 5k, and the total is 12k.
Step 2 — name the invariant. Exactly 8 liters left and exactly 8 liters came back, so the TOTAL never moved. It is 12k before and after. B never moved either.
Step 3 — use the invariant. The new ratio 1:4:7 has 1 + 4 + 7 = 12 parts, and those 12 parts still add to 12k, so one new part is worth exactly k. (This is the whole trick: the same total split into the same number of parts means the part size is unchanged.)
Step 4 — B confirms it: B is 4 new parts = 4k, and B did not change. Consistent.
Step 5 — A is now 1 new part = k, and A is also 3k - 8:
3k - 8 = k
2k = 8
k = 4
Step 6 — original total = 12k = 12 x 4 = 48 liters.
Check: start 12, 16, 20 (total 48). After: 4, 16, 28 (total 48), and 4:16:28 = 1:4:7. Correct.
Answer: 48.
questions.trap: Answering 4 (the value of k) or 12 (the original volume of A) instead of the total. The setup error is subtracting 8 from the total as well - it is an exchange, so the total is invariant, and noticing that is what collapses the three-part algebra into the single equation 3k - 8 = k.

questions.question:
m < 0 and n is not equal to 0
Quantity A: |n^4 + m|
Quantity B: |m - n^4|
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation: Since n is nonzero and 4 is even, n^4 is a strictly positive number. Since m is negative, write |m| = -m, a positive number. Now handle each column. In Quantity B, m - n^4 is a negative number minus a positive number, so it is negative, and removing the bars flips the sign: |m - n^4| = n^4 - m = n^4 + |m|. That is the sum of two positive quantities. In Quantity A, n^4 + m = n^4 - |m|, so Quantity A = |n^4 - |m||, the absolute difference of the same two positive quantities. For any two positive numbers P and Q, |P - Q| is strictly less than P + Q. Therefore Quantity A is always less than Quantity B.
questions.trap: Testing one convenient case such as m = -1 and n = 1, getting Quantity A = 0 and Quantity B = 2, and then answering D because absolute values feel unpredictable. The two columns are structurally the difference and the sum of the same pair of positive numbers, so the sum always wins no matter what m and n are.

questions.question:
In triangle PQR, PQ = 5, QR = 12, and PR = 12.5.
Quantity A: The measure of angle Q, in degrees
Quantity B: The sum of the measures of angles P and R, in degrees
options: C. The two quantities are equal.
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given.
questions.explanation:
1. The angles of a triangle sum to 180, so Quantity B = 180 - (measure of angle Q).
2. So Quantity A < Quantity B exactly when angle Q < 90.
3. Angle Q lies opposite the longest side PR = 12.5. Compare PQ^2 + QR^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 with PR^2 = 156.25.
4. Since 169 > 156.25, the side opposite Q is shorter than it would be in a right triangle, so the angle opposite PR is acute: Q < 90.
5. Therefore Q < 180 - Q, so Quantity B is greater.
Check: with legs 5 and 12, a right angle at Q would need PR = 13. Shortening PR to 12.5 closes the angle at Q, so Q is less than 90 and P + R is more than 90.
questions.trap: Noticing the 5 and 12 sides and assuming a 5-12-13 right triangle gives Q = 90 and P + R = 90, so the quantities look equal (choice C).

questions.question: A trader's profit on item X is 20 percent of the selling price of X, and his profit on item Y is 20 percent of the cost price of Y. The two items have the same selling price, and his total profit on the two items together is $330. By how many dollars does the cost price of Y exceed the cost price of X?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — call the common selling price S and express each profit in terms of S.
Step 2 — item X: profit = 0.20*S directly, since X's profit is a percent of its own selling price. So X's cost is 0.80*S.
Step 3 — item Y: profit = 0.20*CP(Y) and SP = 1.20*CP(Y) = S, so CP(Y) = S/1.20 and the profit is 0.20*S/1.20 = S/6.
Step 4 — add the profits: 0.20*S + S/6 = S/5 + S/6 = 11S/30 = 330, so S = 330*30/11 = $900.
Step 5 — the two cost prices: CP(X) = 0.80*900 = $720 and CP(Y) = 900/1.20 = $750.
Step 6 — CP(Y) - CP(X) = 750 - 720 = $30.
Check the profits: X makes 900 - 720 = $180, and 180/900 = 0.20 of X's selling price; Y makes 900 - 750 = $150, and 150/750 = 0.20 of Y's cost. Together 180 + 150 = $330, as given. Correct.
Answer: 30.
questions.trap: Splitting the $330 evenly, $165 each, which would force the two costs to be equal and give an answer of 0. The two rules do not share a base, so at a common selling price the item priced on its selling price earns MORE (20 percent of S) than the item priced on its cost (S/6, about 16.67 percent of S), and the profits must split 180 to 150. The other slip is reading 'the same selling price' as 'the same cost price' and concluding that the selling prices differ instead.

questions.question: A circle of radius r is rolled inside a circle of radius 4r without slipping. If the small circle starts with its center at distance 3r from the big circle's center, and completes one full trip around the interior of the big circle, how many complete rotations does the small circle make about its own center?
questions.explanation: When a circle of radius r rolls inside a circle of radius R, the small circle's center travels on a circle of radius R − r = 4r − r = 3r. The path length of the small circle's center = 2π(3r). Each full rotation of the small circle covers a distance of 2πr (its circumference). Number of rotations = 2π(3r) / (2πr) = 3. The small circle makes 3 complete rotations.
questions.trap: Using R = 4r as the path radius instead of R − r = 3r, and getting 2π(4r)/(2πr) = 4 rotations.
